Subject: Draft: RFI response and evidence bundle (NIST / EU AI Act / Eval)

Dana / Calyx team — please find our draft RFI response below. I attached two files for your review: rfi_answers_nist_euact.pdf (text responses + mapping tables) and eval_sampling_plan.xlsx (worked example and sample-size calculator).

Key excerpts from the response (summarized):

1) NIST AI RMF mapping- We map Redwood controls to the NIST AI RMF functions as follows: Identify (asset inventory, model registry, model lineage), Protect (RBAC, encryption-in-transit and at-rest, private deployment options), Detect (model performance monitors, anomaly detectors for distribution shift), Respond (rollback policies, canary rollouts, alerting and runbooks), Recover (backup snapshots of models and config, restore procedures). We include control owners and typical evidence locations in the PDF.

2) EU AI Act positioning- Risk classification: the Act's Annex III criteria are use-case centric. For many non-diagnostic NLU features (summarization, search, assisted drafting) the model itself is not automatically "high-risk"; when the model is used to make autonomous decisions affecting safety or fundamental rights (e.g., triage-driven clinical diagnoses), customers should treat the deployment as high-risk. Redwood supports both mitigations and deployment options:
  - Conformity artifacts we can provide: documented intended use, technical documentation (architecture, training-data provenance summaries), post-market monitoring templates, evidence of security testing, and access to inference logs under contractual terms.
  - For customers operating in high-risk categories we recommend private deployments and a compliance staging plan (pre-deploy eval, independent audit-ready artifacts, post-deploy monitoring & periodic re-evaluation).

3) Evaluation and regression approach- We propose a pragmatic, reproducible workflow:
  - Baseline evaluation on curated benchmark and Calyx-provided prompt-sets; metrics: accuracy/coverage for structured outputs, ROUGE/BLEU for specific summarization tasks where applicable, calibrated confidence/error bands for classification-like outputs, and human-in-the-loop error sampling for high-risk items.
  - Regression sampling: trigger-based + periodic sampling. Example: for major model/behavioral releases (>= major weights/version change) sample N examples where N is computed using a binomial proportion confidence interval to detect a delta of X% in an alert metric at 95% CI; the attached XLSX includes the calculator (example assumes baseline error 2.5%, delta 1.5%, target power 0.8).
  - Eval artifacts we can share: example evaluation scripts (Python snippets), dataset manifests, and anonymized sample failures. We can include those scripts as part of the evidence bundle in a mutually agreed S3/Drive share.

Attachments (in this message): rfi_answers_nist_euact.pdf (PDF, 5 pages), eval_sampling_plan.xlsx (XLSX, worked example).

Open items for Calyx: 
- Confirm whether Calyx intends to use the models for triage/automated clinical decisions (that would likely push the use-case into Annex III).
- Confirm an acceptable delivery format for eval scripts (GitHub repo vs. Share Drive vs. isolated artifacts).

We will incorporate any Calyx comments and update the package for final delivery by Thu EOD.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Product Lead, Model Governance
Redwood Inference
